title: Basic 5 · Window / crop (WI)
summary: Pull a sub-window out of an image with the Window node — centred or at an explicit (y, x). SPIDER's WI command.

steps.title: Crop an image
steps.body:
Cutting a small box out of a larger image is called a window (SPIDER's `WI`). cryo-EM uses it for particle boxing (post-picking), pixel-size changes via Fourier cropping, and plain field-of-view restriction.

Leave **`center = ON`** to auto-centre the crop — this is what you want for Fourier cropping (FT → Window → IFT), because the FT output has DC at the centre and a corner-anchored crop would shift DC off-centre.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph so `data.camera` shows its image before cropping.

steps.title: Wire Camera → Window
steps.body: Drag from Camera's `image` output to Window's `image` input.

steps.title: Run the graph to check
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. With default sizes you'll see the default crop — a baseline before setting a sensible size.

steps.title: Click Window
steps.body: Click Window. The Inspector reveals `center` (ON = auto-centre), `ny` / `nx` (crop size), and — only when `center = OFF` — `y` / `x` (top-left anchor).

steps.title: Set nx to 64
steps.body: Enter **64** — the horizontal crop size. The 128² camera image yields a 64² centred crop.

steps.title: Run the graph
steps.body: Press ▶ Run graph. A 64×64 central crop of the camera image appears on the Window node preview.

steps.title: 🎉 Done
steps.body:
**Play with it:**
  - Turn `center` OFF and you can crop from any (y, x) anchor — classic SPIDER WI corner-anchored behaviour, useful when boxing particles from a coordinate file.
  - Real-space crop (big box → small box) restricts the field of view.
  - FT → Window (center=ON) → IFT is the Fourier-crop recipe for coarser pixels / lighter compute.
